Distribution matching and high consistency do not establish individual, subgroup, joint-distribution, network or intervention validity.

Human behavior validation is required when intended outcome is action, not stated intention.

sources.title: Simile — Simulating human behavior
sources.status: Undated official vendor homepage; self-reported validation and customer statements
sources.read_depth: Homepage fetched; validation/refresh/first-party data and customer testimony sections read.
supports: Simile offers population/individual simulations and weekly human validation, >7,000 evaluations across subpopulations/use cases (vendor claim).
Tracks data freshness and recollects on detected drift; first-party loyalty/balance/telemetry data can train custom models (vendor claim).
CVS, Wealthfront, Itaú, Suntory, Gallup are customer/partner names on vendor page, not alternative simulation vendors.
limits: Homepage claims are not independently audited outcomes or evidence of Manager demand.
No public evidence here of reduced suffering or reliable universal counterfactuals.

sources.title: Building confidence in Simile
sources.read_depth: Main methodological sections on TVD, features, confidence models, five-fold evaluation and decision-quality threshold read; no raw benchmark/code audited.
supports: Predict question-level distribution error separately from the behavioral distribution.
~8,600 held-out production-like questions; 5-fold confidence evaluation keeps question text and entire experimental sample in the same fold.
AUROC 0.736 for CFT model vs 0.566 for basic features, on vendor benchmark; RMSE/r reported separately.
TVD 0.16 decision-quality threshold comes from ~2,750 internal ratings by fourteen raters, Fleiss kappa 0.75 over 410 multi-rated questions; not universal.
High-confidence 95% meeting the TVD threshold is a calibrated empirical category, not 95% correctness on all real decisions.
limits: Confidence ranking or a vendor-chosen cutoff is not formal causal calibration or a guarantee under distribution shift.
Cannot compare Aaru AUROC 0.845 vs Simile 0.736 as head-to-head: different evaluation datasets.

sources.title: Population simulation at the replication floor — full research and methodology
sources.status: Vendor technical report/blog; no peer review or independent replication verified
sources.read_depth: Summary and research page fetched; evaluation inputs/cutoff/leakage controls, metrics, sampling adjustment, confidence and claimed behavior comparison read; no source microdata or model execution audited.
supports: 2,993 questions, 13,727 answer shares, nine industries, 186 studies; univariate answer-share accuracy is the explicit main evaluation.
Observed mean TVD 7.62 points and MAE 3.53 points; sampling-adjusted TVD 5.98 and MAE 2.78 are distinct quantities.
Adjustment subtracts expected sampling error, assumes design effect 1, imputes sample size 1,441.5 for 345 questions; not the same as statistical human/LLM calibration.
External retrieval restricted to pages stored at least one day before fieldwork; publisher domains/prediction markets excluded (vendor procedure).
Behavioral brand ranking 92.4% vs survey 77.8% is a vendor-reported separate purchase-panel comparison, not universal human accuracy.
limits: Vendor text explicitly defers higher-order/row-level coherence evidence.
Repeated-survey error range is heterogeneous, not proof of human equivalence for every use.
Correlation r=0.970 is not 97% accuracy.
Reported comparison against Simile uses different benchmarks.
No independent proof of intervention or suffering-reduction validity.

sources.title: Finetuning LLMs for Human Behavior Prediction in Social Science Experiments
sources.status: EMNLP 2025 conference proceedings; formal PDF and landing abstract disagree numerically
sources.read_depth: ACL metadata/abstract plus published PDF pages 1–8 of 16 read. arXiv indexed v2 methods/results passages read. Project site and GitHub README fully read. Appendices pages 9–16 not read; no code/model run.
supports: SocSci210 contains 2.9M responses / 400,491 participants / 210 experiments; unseen studies split 170 train / 40 test.
Published PDF table/arXiv: Qwen SFT Wasserstein distance 0.205→0.151 (26.3% relative reduction); GPT-4o base 0.174, relative reduction13.2%.
Individual response accuracy can worsen while distribution matching improves (Qwen 72.9→69.5).
Reuse public split metadata and SFT/DPO models as validation baselines; choose based on distribution vs individual target.
README uses LLaMA-Factory for finetuning; derived data/models retain their original source licenses; Llama and Qwen terms distinct.
limits: ACL landing abstract says 36%/15%; actual published PDF, project table and arXiv body say 26%/13%; use versioned PDF/table not silently mix.
Project page BibTeX has arXiv2505.10839, inconsistent with official linked paper arXiv2509.05830.
No single unrestricted commercial license established; LICENSE path returned404 but README explicitly describes source terms.
US social-science experiments do not validate another country, minority subgroup, longitudinal life outcome or mental-health effect.

sources.title: LLM Agents Grounded in Self-Reports Enable General-Purpose Simulation of Individuals
sources.status: arXiv preprint, current v3; former 2024 title is not current title
sources.read_depth: Canonical arXiv page/history and exact v3 PDF pages1–12 of86 read; additional indexed methods passages. Remaining74 pages/supplement and public data/code permissions not audited.
supports: 1,052 Americans; two-hour interviews, structured surveys or combined grounding.
Held-out GSS normalized to two-week retest: interview83%, survey82%, combined86%, demographic-only74%. These are relative to retest, not absolute accuracy.
Five experimental replications: authors state design underpowered for comparing effect sizes; simulated effects larger and highly correlated, r0.91–0.99.
Self-reports can outperform demographic role prompts, but outcome reliability and task structure matter.
limits: Survey/retest success is not generic behavior prediction or counterfactual identification.
Real interview burden, consent, source freshness and privacy remain; more data not automatically better.
No direct evidence of reduced suffering.

sources.title: The Illusion of Intervention: Your LLM-Simulated Experiment is an Observational Study
sources.status: arXiv preprint v1; no journal/conference status established in checked canonical page
sources.read_depth: Canonical metadata and arXiv submission history checked; seven indexed in-body passages cover formal selection-bias framing, negative-control diagnosis, targeted confounder adjustment, OpinionQA/book/MovieLens results and limitations. Not full-paper/supplement reading.
supports: Intervention text can shift unspecified latent persona attributes, creating different simulated populations under treatment/control.
Use invariant negative-control outcomes sensitive to omitted attributes to detect drift; compare distributions using TVD and uncertainty.
Adding generic demographics can increase selection bias; targeted task-specific confounders often reduce drift.
Demographic-only negative controls or refusal-dominated outputs can hide drift.
limits: No observed negative-control difference is not proof of no confounding.
Prompt randomization, persona ID copying or temperature seeds do not establish real-human causal effects.
Mitigation is setting/model dependent, not a universal solved problem.

sources.title: This human study did not involve human subjects: Validating LLM simulations as behavioral evidence
sources.read_depth: Canonical metadata and arXiv submission history checked; indexed in-body passages from introduction, §5/PPI and assumptions, exploratory uses and limitations read. Not complete bibliography or all mathematical derivations.
supports: Heuristic repair/finetuning and statistical calibration answer different questions.
PPI combines smaller human labeled sample with larger predicted sample, correcting inference rather than claiming all synthetic subjects interchangeable.
Assumes feature distributions match or valid importance weights; predictor independent from evaluation samples; human gold standard and target population sampling still matter.
Simulate-then-human-validate can prioritize hypotheses, replication studies and design stress tests.
limits: Guarantees are method/assumption dependent, commonly consistency/asymptotic validity, not arbitrary prompt validity.
Precision gains depend on predictive informativeness and can be modest.
Confidence model predicting TVD and sampling-noise subtraction are not substitutes for human-grounded inferential calibration.

sources.title: Code for America: LA flexible interviews
sources.read_depth: Full web article, live fetch maxAge=0; service implementer's account

More than 80 hours shadowing/interviews preceded redesign; county trained 300+ workers; rollout planned for four weeks took many months.
Intervention changed access to a staffed flexible interview line, not merely wording or AI.
limits: Implementer account; early pilot numbers differ from later paper and must not be treated as separate independent replications.
Does not measure subjective suffering or prove an AI tool effect.

sources.title: Administrative Burden and Procedural Denials: Experimental Evidence from SNAP
sources.publisher: Giannella, Homonoff, Rino and Somerville / NBER
sources.published: 2023-05 working paper; 2024 journal version linked, not read
sources.read_depth: Full NBER record plus first 12 of 45 PDF pages (working paper May 2023); introduction, intervention, randomization and data limitations read; later results tables and appendix not read
evidence: 64,798 GetCalFresh applications randomized Oct 2020–May 2021; 48,557 treatment and 16,241 control.
Flexible interviews increased approvals by the 30-day deadline by 6.2 percentage points (13% relative); ever participating by five months +2.2pp; early approvals 14% to 27%.
All participants had already applied; about 2% without phone/email excluded, and repeat applications within 30 days excluded.
No intermediate interview/document submission outcomes; daily status observed for 90 days; reapplications only through GetCalFresh.
limits: Working-paper version read; journal version not read.
Does not establish benefit in a different jurisdiction, different bottleneck, different product or non-applicant population.
S01 and S02 concern the same LA intervention; do not count as independent evidence.

sources.title: Reducing Barriers to SNAP in Boulder County
sources.published: No explicit publication date in extracted body; describes 2023 pilot and April 2024 adoption; metadata modified 2026-06-24
sources.read_depth: Full web article, live fetch
evidence: Three-month RCT, N=1,554, compared mailed status quo to flexible interview option plus three texts.
Benefits arrived 3–4 days sooner; reported additional $100 benefits over initial six months; text delivery cost 97% lower than mailed notices.
Page says approval rate was '6–7% higher' without clarifying relative percentage versus percentage points in this article.
limits: Implementer summary; no independent trial tables read.
Do not convert 6–7% into 6–7 percentage points.
Post-adoption 10% reduction in missed interviews is observational and separate from the RCT.

sources.title: Decreasing SNAP denials due to incomplete information
sources.publisher: U.S. General Services Administration, Office of Evaluation Sciences
sources.published: Publication date not established; study Sep–Dec 2023
sources.read_depth: Full official web summary and all 4 PDF pages
evidence: Randomized N=33,574; basic texts n=16,653, texts with redesigned uploader links n=16,921.
Incomplete-information denials 21.1% to 20.0%, -1.1pp, reported p=.012.
SNAP enrollment 43.3% to 43.8%, +0.5pp, p=.28: no detectable enrollment effect.
30.6% of intervention group uploaded a document via redesigned uploader, so link use alone did not ensure enrollment.
Implementation error meant most received 2 of 7 planned texts; admin data could not measure document upload via any method; bundled design cannot isolate text/access/UI effects.
limits: Null finding is not proof of zero effect; state, design and delivery limit transportability.
Official HTML and PDF reproduce questionable confidence-interval text: enrollment +0.5pp but CI[-0.46,0.15]; do not silently repair or quote those CIs.
Outcome did not directly measure customer experience or suffering.

sources.title: Measuring financial well-being: CFPB user guide

Guide pp12 onward, scoring details and researcher notes not read here; S06 gives official scoring essentials.

sources.title: The World Health Organization-Five Well-Being Index (WHO-5)

Score below 50 suggested as indication for further assessment, not diagnosis.
Document licensed CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO; commercial requests referred to WHO copyright.

For commercial embedding, check rights/license applicability before reuse; public availability alone does not authorize commercial use.
Mental well-being alone does not cover financial, physical, social or environmental welfare; no clinical interpretation by autonomous agent.

sources.title: OECD Guidelines on Measuring Subjective Well-being (2025 Update), Chapter 1
sources.read_depth: Full chapter retrieved; relevant sections on definition, survey design, modes, wording, samples, reporting and interpretation read; not whole book or cited underlying studies
evidence: Subjective well-being comprises life evaluation, affect and eudaimonia; complements objective measures.
Use standardized wording/scales; question placement, survey mode, seasonality and cultural interpretation can affect responses.
Mode always reported; web/phone/in-person differences require attention.
Large population-monitoring samples recommended; mean plus distribution/subgroups, rather than mean alone.
Causal analyses must consider omitted variables, reverse causality, adaptation and shared method variance.
limits: National-statistics sample guidance is not a power calculation for a startup pilot.
Human subjective reports; no justified interspecies utility conversion.
